intent: I have worn artificial turf at a home, on HOA common land or on a business site in the Denver metro. Can I replace it after Colorado's 2026 rules, what does the new turf have to meet, does my city review a replacement or require worn turf to be replaced, and does Thornton's rebate help?
distinctValue: The national replacement page is generic about approvals. This page answers the replacement-specific question for the Denver metro: does the job fall under state and city rules at an existing property? (1) C.R.S. 25-15-605 (SB24-081) bars installing artificial turf with intentionally added PFAS on any property from 1 January 2026 and protects maintaining pre-2026 turf; SB24-081 does not define maintaining, and SB24-005 defines it for article 99 as preserving the existing state of installed turf, so the page tells the reader to plan on the new turf meeting the PFAS rule. (2) Per city, whether the landscape code reaches a replacement at an existing property: Northglenn 11-4-7(b)(4)(B) exempts site landscaping improvements at existing single-family, duplex and manufactured homes except (d) and (e)(1), and (e)(1)(E) allows artificial ground cover 'pursuant to' the turf regulations, whose (f)(3), (4) and (6) include the replacement duty; Brighton 8.01 exempts repairs and improvements to detached houses and duplexes not under Site Improvement / Residential Design Review and existing-development work under 10%, with 8.04's percolation and replacement rules applying only where the standards apply; Thornton Water's 2026 rebate rules require a Minor Development Permit before installing turf as landscaping, define PFAS-free strictly, let a product later found to contain PFAS stay if documentation was complied with, list replacement in maintenance, and limit the rebate to turf replacing high-water lawn or bare new-construction ground; Westminster's 2004 regulations (replacement when the City determines turf no longer mimics a healthy lawn), its April 2025 FAQ (back-yard turf installed in practice without City review; ODP amendment for HOA common areas, commercial sites and rights of way; the rewrite is prospective and not retroactive) and its May 2026 public review draft (landscape chapter reaches existing development without a landscaping ODP when landscaping changes by the greater of 200 square feet or five percent; turf in rear yards and recreation areas; four-foot planted buffer). (3) For HOA and business land, the SB24-005 / HB25-1113 redevelopment test and functional-turf definition, briefly, with the guide linked. Town pages cover each city's install rules for a new lawn; the residential page covers Brighton 8.01 for front yards; the sports-field page covers Boulder's carve-out and Westminster's draft for fields. None asks whether a replacement at an existing property is inside each city's code.

sources.label: Colorado General Assembly: SB24-081 signed act PDF (curl, pdftotext; 7 pages)
supports: 25-15-605. Prohibition on the installation of artificial turf that contains intentionally added PFAS chemicals. (1) ON AND AFTER JANUARY 1, 2026, A PERSON SHALL NOT INSTALL ARTIFICIAL TURF THAT CONTAINS INTENTIONALLY ADDED PFAS CHEMICALS ON ANY PORTION OF PROPERTY IN THE STATE.
(2) NOTHING IN THIS SECTION PROHIBITS A PERSON FROM MAINTAINING ARTIFICIAL TURF INSTALLED BEFORE JANUARY 1, 2026.

Section 5 adds 25-15-605 and does not define maintaining or artificial turf; the page therefore makes no claim about which parts of a turf system the rule reaches, and advises asking whether the maker's statement covers backing and infill.

sources.label: Colorado General Assembly: SB24-005 signed act PDF (curl, pdftotext; 7 pages)
supports: 37-99-102(10) "MAINTAIN" OR "MAINTAINING" MEANS AN ACTION TO PRESERVE THE EXISTING STATE OF NONFUNCTIONAL TURF, ARTIFICIAL TURF, OR AN INVASIVE PLANT SPECIES THAT HAS ALREADY BEEN INSTALLED, PLANTED, OR PLACED.
37-99-102(9) "LOCAL ENTITY" MEANS A: (a) HOME RULE OR STATUTORY CITY, COUNTY, CITY AND COUNTY, TERRITORIAL CHARTER CITY, OR TOWN; (b) SPECIAL DISTRICT; AND (c) METROPOLITAN DISTRICT.

37-99-102(5) "COMMON INTEREST COMMUNITY PROPERTY" MEANS PROPERTY WITHIN A COMMON INTEREST COMMUNITY THAT IS OWNED AND MAINTAINED BY A UNIT OWNERS' ASSOCIATION, SUCH AS ENTRYWAYS, PARKS, AND OTHER COMMON ELEMENTS AS DEFINED IN SECTION 38-33.3-103 (5).

37-99-102(14) "REDEVELOPMENT PROJECT" MEANS A CONSTRUCTION PROJECT THAT: (a) REQUIRES A BUILDING OR LANDSCAPING PERMIT, PLAN CHECK, OR DESIGN REVIEW; AND (b) RESULTS IN A DISTURBANCE OF MORE THAN FIFTY PERCENT OF THE AGGREGATE LANDSCAPE AREA.

37-99-103(4) NOTHING IN THIS SECTION PROHIBITS: (a) A LOCAL ENTITY FROM MAINTAINING, OR ALLOWING ANY PERSON TO MAINTAIN, ANY NONFUNCTIONAL TURF, ARTIFICIAL TURF, OR INVASIVE PLANT SPECIES INSTALLED, PLANTED, OR PLACED BEFORE JANUARY 1, 2026; ... (d) ... MORE STRINGENT THAN THE REQUIREMENTS OF THIS SECTION; OR (e) A LOCAL ENTITY OR THE DEPARTMENT FROM INSTALLING, OR ALLOWING ANY PERSON TO INSTALL, ARTIFICIAL TURF ON ATHLETIC FIELDS OF PLAY.

(6.5) "FUNCTIONAL ARTIFICIAL TURF" MEANS ARTIFICIAL TURF THAT IS: (a) LOCATED IN A RECREATIONAL USE AREA OR OTHER SPACE THAT IS REGULARLY USED FOR CIVIC, COMMUNITY, OR RECREATIONAL PURPOSES, WHICH MAY INCLUDE A PLAYGROUND, A SPORTS FIELD, A PICNIC GROUND, AN AMPHITHEATER, A PORTION OF A PARK, AND THE PLAYING AREA OF A GOLF COURSE ...

37-99-103(4)(a) as amended: A local entity from maintaining, or allowing any person to maintain, any nonfunctional turf, NONFUNCTIONAL ARTIFICIAL TURF, artificial turf, or invasive plant species installed, planted, or placed before January 1, 2026.

sources.label: Northglenn Municipal Code, Article 11-4 Development Standards, section 11-4-7 (curl; section source note Ord. 1766, 2019; 1782, 2019; 1848, 2023; 1870, 2025)
supports: (b) Applicability. (1) New Development. Unless otherwise exempted in Subsection 11-4-7(b)(3) below, or elsewhere in this UDO, the standards in Section 11-4-7 shall apply to all new development and land uses. (2) Expansions and Enlargements. ... the standards in Section 11-4-7 shall apply to the following expansions and enlargements: (A) Any site improvements requiring full compliance pursuant to 11-1-5(f)(3) ... (B) The expansion or enlargement of a use or structure that requires a special use permit; or (C) Major parking area improvements ...

(4) Exemptions. The standards in Section 11-4-7 shall not apply to the following: ... (B) Site landscaping improvements on properties with existing single-family, duplex, or manufactured home dwellings, except that such improvements shall comply with 11-4-7(d), Site Area Landscaping, and 11-4-7(e)(1), Appropriate Landscaping Materials;

Numbering note: the posted text lists (b)(3) Replacement of Existing Screening and (b)(4) Exemptions, although (b)(1) and (b)(2) refer to exemptions in (b)(3). The page names no subsection number for the exemption.

(d) Required Site Area Landscaping. ... For existing single family attached and detached residential, only the appropriate landscaping materials section outlined in Section 11-4-7(e)(1)(A-E) below is applicable.

(e)(1) Appropriate Landscaping Materials. Required landscaped areas pursuant to Subsection 11-4-7(d), above, may include the following landscaping materials: ... (E) Artificial ground cover, pursuant to subsection 11-4-7(F), artificial turf regulations;

(f)(3) Installation: Artificial turf shall be installed in accordance with the manufacturer's specifications and maintained in a manner to mimic healthy living turf, including the following: (A) Sod or existing groundcover shall be removed prior to installation of any artificial turf. (B) Artificial turf shall be installed over a compacted and porous road base material. (C) Artificial turf shall be anchored at all edges and seams.
(4) Slope restrictions: Artificial turf shall not be installed on slopes greater than six percent.
(6) Maintenance: The following maintenance activities are required for artificial turf; ... replacement of the artificial turf when maintenance or repair is unable to simulate a healthy living turf.

sources.label: City of Brighton Land Use code, Article 8, 8.01 Intent and Applicability (Municode, headless Chromium; Ord. No. 2438, § 13, 1-2-2024)
supports: Applicability. The standards of this Section shall apply to all new development except:

Improvements or repairs to detached houses and duplexes that are not subject to a Site Improvement / Residential Design Review as provided in Section 2.05, and which are not part of a larger residential neighborhood or subdivision plan; and

Improvements or repairs to existing development that do not result in an increase in building footprint or impervious surfaces by more than 10% or changes in use that do not result in an increase in intensity.

In cases where improvements or repairs increase the building footprint or impervious surface by more than 10% or changes intensity of use, the intent is to bring the site into full compliance with these standards, except that the Director may prorate the requirements ...

sources.label: City of Brighton Land Use code, Article 8, 8.04 Plant Specifications (Municode, headless Chromium; Ord. No. 2438, §§ 21-24, 1-2-2024)
supports: Artificial Turf: The chosen material and any underlayment installed below the turf shall have a minimum percolation rate of 5 inches per hour. The liner material and all bedding shall be permeable to allow for infiltration of water into the soil below to mimic conditions of sod and natural grasses.
Artificial turf shall be cleaned and debris removed on a regular basis. Artificial turf shall be replaced when it is no longer simulating the infiltration properties of sod or native grasses.

sources.label: Thornton Water: 2026 Artificial Turf Rules for Water-Wise Landscape Rebate, Information and Requirements (PDF, curl and pdftotext; 6 pages, each footed 1/1/2026)
supports: Design Requirements ... 1. A Minor Development Permit is required before the installation of artificial turf as landscaping.

PFAS-free means that at least one of the following requirements have been met: 1. The manufacturer or distributor has publicly stated that the product is made without the intentional use of PFAS in a statement referring to all members of the class of PFAS ... "PFC-free" shall not be sufficient to satisfy this requirement.

2. The product has been tested and shown to be PFAS-free. Testing sufficient to satisfy this requirement may have been carried out at the manufacturer's request or as a part of an independent investigation ... Testing completed by the manufacturer does not satisfy this requirement. Testing results must be published online ...
3. Documentation showing that the proposed product is PFAS-free shall be submitted at the time of permit application ...
5. If a product is installed that is later determined to contain PFAS, it may remain in place if the applicant complies with the PFAS-free documentation requirements.
General Maintenance ... 6. Replacement of the artificial turf when maintenance or repair cannot simulate a healthy living turf.

Rebate Requirements 1. ... To be eligible for the rebate, artificial turf must replace an area of high-water demand lawn, such as Kentucky Bluegrass, on existing residential lots or areas of no landscaping on new construction residential lots.
2. A Minor Development Permit approval is required before installing artificial turf as landscaping. Please contact the Planning Department's Planner of the Day for details.

sources.label: City of Westminster: Landscape Regulations 2004 (PDF, curl, pdftotext, pdfinfo; 46 pages, PDF created 24 April 2017)
supports: City of Westminster Landscape Regulations Effective Date September 1, 2004 2004 Edition
The use of artificial turf is generally prohibited, except for use in single-family detached or duplex lot yard areas not adjacent to a street, or public or private park or open space.

Artificial turf shall be installed according to industry specifications and maintained in a manner to mimic a healthy living turf. Replacement of artificial turf shall be required when the material, wear, or installation is such that it is determined by the City that it no longer visually mimics a healthy living lawn area.

sources.label: City of Westminster: Landscape Changes Frequently Asked Questions (PDF, curl, pdftotext; 4 pages, PDF created 14 April 2025)
supports: The regulations were last updated in 2004 as a result of concerns coming out of the 2002 drought. ... These regulations are being updated as part of the scope of work for larger Unified Development Code project ... The updated regulations are prospective with new development and not retroactive.

Artificial turf is allowed in single unit and duplex type development, when not adjacent to a street, park or open space. In practice this has allowed residents to install artificial turf in back yard areas without restrictions nor the need for City review.
ODP landscape amendments are required in locations outside of a homeowner's private property such as HOA common areas, within commercial development, or within public rights of way.

sources.label: City of Westminster: Unified Development Code, May 2026 Public Review Draft (Planning Commission Packet Addendum June 23, 2026; PDF, curl, pdftotext; 566 pages, printed 06/18/2026)
supports: 11-1-2(B) This Title shall become effective on ______ (Effective Date).

11-7-1(B)(1)(a) This chapter provides minimum design, installation, irrigation, and maintenance criteria for landscape improvements on private property. The standards in this chapter shall apply to the following: (i) New development; (ii) Existing developments with an ODP that addresses landscaping, where landscaping is proposed to be modified from what was approved or there is an increase in any aspect of nonconformance with this Title; (iii) Existing developments without an approved ODP or ODP Waiver that addresses landscaping, where landscaping is proposed to be changed by at least 200 square feet or five percent, whichever is greater; or (iv) Existing multiunit, commercial, industrial, and office developments where an ODP or ODP Waiver exists but does not address the landscape that is proposed to be modified.

11-7-1(D)(3)(k)(ii) Permitted Locations. Artificial turf is permitted as follows: a) Within rear yard areas of lots with single unit detached and attached structures. b) In any zoning district where used for community gathering or recreational purposes such as playgrounds, pet relief areas, amphitheaters, active play or athletic areas in parks, or the greens within golf courses.

(v) Buffering a) A minimum four-foot buffer shall be provided between the edge of the artificial turf and any impervious surface. ... c) The required buffer shall be planted with any combination of ornamental trees, shrubs, vines, groundcover, perennial or annual flowers, or ornamental grasses.

unresolved: SB24-081 does not define maintaining, and SB24-005's definition (preserving the existing state of installed turf) is written for article 99. Neither law says whether a full strip-and-relay is maintenance or a new installation. The page says neither law spells it out and tells the reader to plan on the new turf meeting the PFAS rule.
